unit_description: This unit builds the foundation for working with whole numbers through 100,000. Students learn what a digit's place means, build numbers with base-ten models, write numbers in standard and expanded form, and read and write numbers in words.
unit_goals: Understand that a digit's value depends on its place.
Build and draw numbers with base-ten models.
Write numbers in standard, expanded, and word form.
Use place-value language to describe and compare numbers.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students learn that digits have different values depending on their position, build numbers with base-ten models, and connect standard, expanded, and word forms.

lessons.lesson_title: What a Digit's Place Tells Us
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by counting by tens and hundreds on a number line.
lessons.concept: A digit's value changes by place. In 333, the left 3 means 300, the middle 3 means 30, and the right 3 means 3.
lessons.practice: Match digits in a number to their place-value labels and tell the value of each digit.
lessons.objective: Understand that a digit's value depends on its place in a number.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by naming the value of the underlined digit.

questions.prompt: In 45__6__, what is the value of the underlined digit?
questions.hint: The 4 is in the hundreds place.

questions.prompt: In __3__72, what is the value of the underlined digit?
questions.hint: The 3 is in the thousands place.

learn.title: What a Digit's Place Tells Us
teaching_points: The same digit has a different value depending on where it sits.
A place-value chart helps us read the value of each digit.

example.prompt: In the number 5,328, what does the digit 3 stand for?
example.equation: 3 is in the hundreds place, so it means 300.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: The 7 is in the thousands place.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Name the value of each underlined digit.

flashcards.title: Place-Value Vocabulary
flashcards.instructions: Review place-value words and digit values.

bigIdea.title: What a Digit's Place Tells Us
bigIdea.subtitle: The same digit can mean different amounts
bigIdea.intro: The number 333 uses the same digit three times, but each 3 means a different amount because it sits in a different place.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does the same digit mean different amounts?

ruleCards.description: The digit in the ones place shows how many single units.
The digit in the tens place is worth ten times as much as the same digit in the ones place.

lessons.fact_drill: Quickly identify hundreds, tens, and ones from base-ten pictures.
lessons.concept: Use base-ten blocks to model numbers: small cubes for ones, rods for tens, flats for hundreds, and large cubes for thousands.
lessons.practice: Build a number with base-ten blocks and write it in standard form.
lessons.objective: Use base-ten models to represent numbers.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by counting base-ten blocks.

questions.prompt: 1 ten rod equals how many ones cubes?
questions.hint: A ten rod is made of ten ones.

questions.prompt: 1 hundred flat equals how many ten rods?
questions.hint: A hundred flat is ten ten-rods wide.

questions.prompt: If you have 2 tens and 5 ones, what number do you build?

learn.title: Build Numbers With Base-Ten Models
teaching_points: A flat square is one hundred.
A large cube is one thousand.

example.prompt: Use blocks to show the number 243.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: You have 1 hundred flat, 3 ten rods, and 6 ones cubes. What number did you build?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Match base-ten models to the numbers they show.

flashcards.title: Base-Ten Models
flashcards.instructions: Review base-ten block names and values.

bigIdea.title: Build Numbers With Base-Ten Models
bigIdea.subtitle: Use blocks to see what numbers mean
bigIdea.intro: Numbers are made of ones, tens, hundreds, and thousands. Base-ten blocks let you see and touch each part of a number.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do base-ten blocks show a number?

ruleCards.description: When you have ten ones, trade them for one ten rod.
When you have ten ten rods, trade them for one hundred flat.

lessons.lesson_title: Write Numbers in Standard and Expanded Form
lessons.fact_drill: Practice writing numbers from base-ten pictures.
lessons.concept: Standard form is the usual way to write a number. Expanded form shows the value of each digit added together.
lessons.practice: Convert numbers between standard and expanded form.
lessons.objective: Write numbers in standard and expanded form.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by breaking a number into parts.

questions.prompt: What is the value of the 6 in 6,214?
questions.hint: The 6 is in the thousands place.

learn.title: Standard and Expanded Form
teaching_points: Standard form writes a number the usual way.
Expanded form adds the value of each digit.
Expanded form helps show why a digit's place matters.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: There are 0 tens, so skip that part.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Switch numbers between standard and expanded form.

flashcards.title: Standard and Expanded Form
flashcards.instructions: Practice matching standard and expanded forms.

bigIdea.title: Write Numbers in Standard and Expanded Form
bigIdea.subtitle: Show the value of each digit
bigIdea.intro: Standard form is the quick way we usually write numbers. Expanded form pulls the number apart so you can see each digit's value.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How does expanded form show a digit's value?

ruleCards.description: The compact way to write a number using digits.
The number written as the sum of each digit's value.

lessons.lesson_title: Read and Write Numbers in Words
lessons.fact_drill: Write three numbers in expanded form as a warm-up.
lessons.concept: Number words use commas and hyphens to match the digits in a number. Read from left to right, naming each period.
lessons.practice: Convert numbers to words and words to numbers.
lessons.objective: Read and write numbers using words.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Warm up by writing numbers in words.

questions.hint: Use a hyphen for the tens and ones.

learn.title: Read and Write Numbers in Words
teaching_points: Name the thousands or hundreds period first.
Use hyphens between twenty-one and ninety-nine.
Use 'and' only for separating whole numbers from decimals, not for whole numbers.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.hint: One thousand, then twenty-four with a hyphen.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Write numbers in words and write word names as numbers.

flashcards.title: Number Words
flashcards.instructions: Practice reading and writing numbers in words.

bigIdea.title: Read and Write Numbers in Words
bigIdea.subtitle: Use words to name numbers
bigIdea.intro: Numbers can be written with digits or words. Writing them in words helps us slow down and think about what each part means.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How do commas and hyphens help write numbers?

ruleCards.description: Use hyphens when writing numbers from twenty-one to ninety-nine.
Commas separate the thousands, millions, and other periods.

lessons.fact_drill: Rapid review of digit values, base-ten models, expanded form, and number words.
lessons.concept: Review what a digit's place tells us, base-ten models, standard and expanded form, and number words.
lessons.practice: Complete a balanced evaluation covering the skills from this unit.
lessons.objective: Show what you know about place value foundations.

warmup.title: Luma Charge
warmup.instructions: Get ready to show what you know.

questions.prompt: What is the value of 2 in 2,405?
questions.hint: The 2 is in the thousands place.
Use a hyphen between seventy and two.

learn.title: Ready to Show What You Know
teaching_points: Use base-ten models or expanded form if you get stuck.

example.prompt: You have learned four big ideas this unit.
example.equation: digit value + base-ten models + expanded form + number words = place value foundations

practice_block.title: Unit Evaluation
practice_block.instructions: Answer all questions carefully to show your understanding.

flashcards.title: Unit 1 Review
flashcards.instructions: Review key terms from Unit 1 before the evaluation.

bigIdea.title: Unit Evaluation: Place Value Foundations
bigIdea.subtitle: Show what you know
bigIdea.intro: This evaluation checks your understanding of the four big ideas from this unit: digit values, base-ten models, expanded form, and number words.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: What do you know about place value?

ruleCards.equation: A digit's place tells its value
ruleCards.description: Remember that the same digit can mean different amounts depending on its place.
The same number can be written in standard form, expanded form, or words.
